questions.cardText:
[Zoology] How do ogre-faced spiders hear?
A. Through their eyes
B. By vibrating their webs
C. Using their hairs and legs
Answer: C. Ogre-faced spiders, despite not having ears, can detect sounds using specialized receptors on their legs. Their remarkable hearing allows them to catch flying insects midair even while blindfolded by researchers.
questions.de: Kescherspinnen (Deinopis) haben keine Ohren – mit welchen Körperteilen nehmen sie Geräusche wahr?
questions.en: Ogre-faced spiders have no ears – with which body parts do they detect sounds?

timeline.labelEn: A study in Current Biology shows ogre-faced spiders use sound to detect airborne prey
timeline.labelDe: Eine Studie in Current Biology zeigt, dass Kescherspinnen fliegende Beute am Geräusch erkennen

questions.notes: Card correct: Deinopis uses hairs and slit sensilla on its legs to detect sounds up to 2 m away (Stafstrom et al. 2020).

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Invention] In which decade was the first electric car commercially sold?
A. 1890s
B. 1940s
C. 1990s
Answer: A. One of the first commercially sold electric cars is the Electrobat. This electric vehicle was notably used for taxis in New York City and became quite popular in the 1890s.
questions.de: Welches frühe Elektroauto, 1894 von Henry G. Morris und Pedro G. Salom aus Philadelphia patentiert, fuhr als Elektrotaxi in New York City?
questions.en: Which early electric car, patented in 1894 by Henry G. Morris and Pedro G. Salom of Philadelphia, ran as electric cabs in New York City?

timeline.labelEn: The Electrobat, one of the first electric automobiles, receives its patent
timeline.labelDe: Das Electrobat, eines der ersten Elektroautos, erhält sein Patent

questions.notes: Card's decade claim is shaky: Wikipedia's Electric car article lists Thomas Parker's car (1884) and the Flocken Elektrowagen (1888), so the first electric cars predate the 1890s; the Electrobat (1894) was only 'one of the first'. Reworked to the Electrobat itself.
